questions.q: Why does the product-images container need to be created before anything can be uploaded?
options: Blob storage needs a container as the namespace that will actually hold the blobs
Storage accounts can only hold one file each
Containers are only needed for files larger than 1 GB
Azure requires a container name to match the storage account name
questions.explain: A blob container is the namespace inside a storage account where the actual objects live -- it has to exist before anything can be uploaded into it.

questions.q: Why is the Hot access tier the right choice for Driftwood's product images?
options: Hot is the cheapest tier, which is the only consideration that matters
Images viewed constantly by shoppers need lowest access cost and no retrieval delay, which is exactly what Hot provides
Archive tier is required for any image file
Cool tier cannot store image files
questions.explain: The tradeoff is always lower storage cost for higher access cost and latency. Product images read constantly are the textbook case for Hot, since Cool or Archive would add latency or a multi-hour rehydration delay neither customers nor the deadline can afford.

questions.q: What does `az storage blob upload-batch` do that uploading each image individually would not?
options: It automatically resizes every image for the web
It uploads every file in a local folder to the container in one command, the practical choice for hundreds of product photos
It converts images to a different file format during upload
It deletes the on-prem copies automatically
questions.explain: upload-batch moves an entire local folder's contents into a container in one command, rather than requiring a separate upload command per file.

questions.q: What does "pointing the app at the new location" actually require?
options: Nothing -- moving the files is sufficient on its own
Updating the app's image-rendering logic to build URLs from the storage account's blob endpoint instead of the old local file path
Reinstalling the catalog app from scratch
Renaming every image file to match a new naming convention
questions.explain: Every blob has a predictable public URL built from the storage account and container name; the app's code needs to build URLs in that shape instead of the old local path.

questions.q: Why isn't an upload command finishing without an error proof that the migration worked?
options: It is proof -- no further validation is needed
Because it only proves the upload didn't fail, not that every file arrived correctly or that the app can actually use the new URLs -- that needs a count check, a spot check, and an app check
Because Azure CLI commands never report errors accurately
Because uploaded files are automatically deleted after 24 hours unless manually confirmed
questions.explain: Real validation means a count check (blob count matches source file count), a spot check (images actually load and look correct), and an app check (the app renders them from their new URLs).
